text:
Ben Bolt I now understand the misunderstanding was your part and not theirs. They are talking about recommendation letters from Israelis and suggested some alternatives for you. This has nothing to do with the marriage, like you put it in the original post.

The partner immigration process requires recommendation letters from Israeli citizens, who can attest that the relationship is genuine. If you don't know any Israeli, so proceed without it. 
This also has nothing to do with the marriage. You can get married whenever you want. Marriage is not a condition for the partner immigration process.
